market_mood: Markets are tense and risk-off ahead of Nvidia's earnings, with tech leading a broad pullback, while housing data hit a 14-year low and Middle East tensions with Iran keep simmering.
self_check: My high-confidence calls have badly underperformed (3 of 14) and oil ideas have been poor lately, while consumer, merger and rate ideas held up best, so today I used no high confidence, avoided energy, and leaned on consumer and deal-driven ideas.

picks.reason: Anthropic's IPO is reportedly pricing above a $1.5 trillion valuation, and Amazon is one of its largest backers plus its main compute partner, a stake value the market hasn't fully reflected.
Nike holds its first investor day in nine years to lay out turnaround targets, and such multi-year plans tend to keep re-rating a stock over following weeks rather than in one session.
Homebuilder sentiment fell to a 14-1/2-year low with more builders cutting prices, a sign housing-linked demand for big-ticket home products stays weak.
Carlisle is buying insulated metal panel maker PermaTherm, a bolt-on that adds to its commercial building envelope business away from weak residential demand.
Repair-and-remodel supplier squeezed by a frozen housing market and rising input costs.

watchlist_notes.note: Index is down 4.7% in a month and fell again ahead of Nvidia's results, which are the next big swing factor.
Nasdaq names are the epicenter of the de-risking into Nvidia's print and the Anthropic IPO.
Dow slid as software stocks sagged despite a decent retail sales number.
Reportedly close to a rare 4-5 year DRAM supply deal with Samsung, locking in memory amid an AI-driven shortage.
Named among hyperscalers lobbying against Trump's proposed China data center curbs, a policy risk to watch.
Earnings tonight are the market's key AI test; the stock has already sold off into it, so the reaction could go either way.
Its Anthropic stake is being marked up by an IPO reportedly pricing above a $1.5 trillion valuation.
Holds an Anthropic stake and TPU momentum, though Druckenmiller exited his position last quarter.
Part of the failed lobbying push against China data center restrictions.
Committing $3.3 billion to expand its German plant for Cybercab production starting 2029.
A software bug froze Chase consumer banking for hours, an operational embarrassment but not financially material.
Oil is stuck between Gulf tanker attacks and rising Middle East exports, keeping energy the week's best sector.
Gold is steady with a firm dollar offsetting Iran-related geopolitical bids.
Soft homebuilder sentiment and moderate retail sales keep the rate-cut debate alive for long bonds.

top_buys.pitch: Anthropic's blockbuster IPO marks up a stake Amazon holds at a fraction of today's value.
top_buys.why: Anthropic is reportedly pricing its IPO above a $1.5 trillion valuation on frenzied demand, and Amazon is one of its biggest investors and its key compute partner. A public mark creates a visible, quantifiable asset on Amazon's balance sheet that most investors haven't modeled. Unlike a one-day headline pop, the actual listing and lock-up discussion should keep this in the news for weeks.
top_buys.risks: If Nvidia's results disappoint, the whole AI complex including Amazon sells off regardless of the Anthropic stake; proposed China data center curbs are another overhang.
top_buys.watch: Anthropic's IPO pricing and first trading day, plus Nvidia's earnings reaction.

top_buys.pitch: First investor day in nine years is a chance to reset expectations for the turnaround.
top_buys.why: Nike is hosting its first investor day since 2017 to show that its rightsizing and product reset are working. These events typically come with multi-year margin and revenue targets that analysts digest and upgrade against over following weeks. Consumer-facing ideas have been my most reliable category lately, and retail sales came in moderately positive.
top_buys.risks: If management sets conservative targets or flags more inventory cleanup, the stock can fade hard; a weak tape makes any disappointment worse.
top_buys.watch: The financial targets issued at the investor day and any analyst upgrades/downgrades that follow.

top_buys.pitch: Housing demand keeps deteriorating, and the biggest home-improvement retailer feels it with a lag.
top_buys.why: Builder sentiment just hit a 14-1/2-year low, with high mortgage rates and rising material, labor and energy costs forcing more price cuts. That environment points to a soft spring for construction and remodel spending, which drives Home Depot's pro business. The market tends to underreact to slow-burn housing data compared with headline events.
top_buys.risks: A dovish rate turn or falling mortgage rates would quickly revive housing-linked stocks; Home Depot is a defensive mega-cap that may hold up in a selloff.
top_buys.watch: Home Depot's next quarterly results and commentary, plus housing starts and mortgage rate trends.

top_buys.pitch: Bolt-on acquisition extends Carlisle's commercial building envelope franchise at a time residential is the weak spot.
top_buys.why: Carlisle agreed to buy PermaTherm, an insulated metal panel maker, deepening its energy-efficient building products line. Small, accretive bolt-ons are how Carlisle has compounded, and the market rarely prices them in immediately. Its exposure skews to commercial re-roofing, which is less tied to the collapsing homebuilder sentiment.
top_buys.risks: If construction weakness spreads from residential to commercial, Carlisle's end markets soften and the deal won't matter.
top_buys.watch: Deal close terms and any update to Carlisle's full-year guidance.

top_buys.pitch: Repair-and-remodel supplier squeezed by a frozen housing market and rising input costs.
top_buys.why: Builder sentiment at a 14-year low with widespread price cuts signals weak demand for paint, plumbing and cabinetry products. Masco also faces higher labor and material costs noted in the same survey. Housing-linked industrial names tend to grind lower as the data keeps disappointing.
top_buys.risks: Masco is already cheap and a rate-cut narrative could lift the whole housing complex quickly.
top_buys.watch: Housing starts, mortgage rates and Masco's next guidance update.

summary.big_story: Stocks fell again ahead of Nvidia's make-or-break AI earnings, while US homebuilder sentiment collapsed to a 14-year low.
summary.top_pick: Amazon, because Anthropic's IPO pricing above a $1.5 trillion valuation quietly marks up Amazon's stake and its cloud relationship.
summary.watch: Nvidia's results and guidance after the close, plus Nike's investor day targets.
